doc.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: John Lewis as an economical accompanist
summary: Heath describes John Lewis's playing in Dizzy's band, his part on Two Bass Hit, and the early Milt Jackson quartet.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did John sound like John Lewis on piano?
John Lewis always sounded like John.
From Dizzy Gillespie’s band, he was economical and still he fed the soloist.
So he was a great accompanist?

He was a great accompanist from the moment we heard him. He did something on “Two Bass Hit” behind Ray Brown that everybody was saying, “Listen to John Lewis behind that!” [sings] Some kind of rhythmic thing he set up when the band came in after Brown’s solo. John Lewis has always been a phenomenal pianist! He went with Ella, too. At the early stages of the quartet, we weren’t doing anything. No jobs. We were Milt Jackson’s quartet actually at that time. But I’m jumping ahead a little bit because…
